title: RAW UNREVIEWED: wind names form a four-leg route with quality carried to each next sector
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Try a medieval navigational reading of a wind-rose sequence: four heading sectors each organize a three-name wind leg; a written quality attached to a named wind carries to the next described sector as the travel condition. The source-side unit is the complete BnF Latin 18499 f.67v2 inscription, including all four headings, twelve wind names, and four quality pairs. The candidate target unit, if already eligible, is the complete f69r folio and all its 22 written loci; no geometry, target text, or new image was accessed for this proposal. Existing GDT1067 leaves source/destination polarity non-identifiable from geometry alone, so a later reading requires an independently written direction/sequence cue and may not infer flow from radial arrangement. Rival: a static wind taxonomy grouped for mnemonic display, with no itinerary or carried state. Which sectors, names, or quality groups correspond remains unknown.

design.mechanism: A directional heading starts each of four ordered route legs; three wind-name positions fill successive path stages and an attached quality describes the air encountered at that stage and carried into the next transition.
design.unit: Complete BnF Latin 18499 f.67v2 source inscription (four headings, twelve wind names, four quality pairs) and, only if its existing access grant permits, the complete already-exposed f69r folio with all 22 loci.
design.contrast: Sequential route with wind-quality state transitions versus a static wind-name/quality taxonomy; also distinguish textual direction from radial orientation alone.
design.prediction: A future whole target reading must retain a consistent order through all eligible sectors and carry each quality only where the text connects it; no single geometry-based origin/destination choice may be used. If written transition cues are absent, report no directional capacity and keep the catalogue rival.
design.scope: No new target access. f69r's admitted status and exact written cue capacity remain unverified for this idea; GDT1067's polarity limit is not reopened.
